name: CR-Diff-09-misc-2.b
generalfeedback:
To solve this problem you will need to use the product rule <hint>calc_product_rule</hint> and the quotient rule<hint>calc_quotient_rule</hint>.

Let \(f({{CT:0}})={{CT:2}}\) and \(g({{CT:0}})={{CT:3}}\). Then,

\[\frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:1}}\right] = \frac{\frac{df}{d{{CT:0}}}\cdot g - f\cdot \frac{dg}{d{{CT:0}}}}{g^2}.\]

In order to calculate \(\frac{dg}{d{{CT:0}}}\) you need to use the product rule, by defining two new functions: \(h({{CT:0}})={{CT:0}}\) and \(i({{CT:0}})={{CT:4}}\) so that \(g({{CT:0}})=h({{CT:0}})i({{CT:0}})\).

So,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[{{CT:3}}] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{dh}{d{{CT:0}}}\cdot i + h\cdot \frac{di}{d{{CT:0}}}\\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  [{{CT:5}}]{{CT:4}} + {{CT:0}}[{{CT:6}}] \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:7}}
 \end{array}\]

Hence,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:1}}\right] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{\frac{df}{d{{CT:0}}}\cdot g - f\cdot \frac{dg}{d{{CT:0}}}}{g^2} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{[{{CT:8}}]{{CT:4}} - {{CT:2}}[{{CT:6}}]}{[{{CT:4}}]^2} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{{{CT:9}} - {{CT:10}}}{{CT:11}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:12}}
 \end{array}\]
